name: Hands
description: Makes sure a system's enduring integrations, such as an enterprise system's own AI tool registry, its LLM platform and its guardrails, are appropriately accessible to the system and used by it. The language models and guardrails themselves come from World, and generic tool calling such as MCP belongs to World as well. Specified to expect adaptation to a particular system.
purpose: Make the integrations a system already depends on accessible to the AI and actually used.
approach: Read the system's declaration of its integrations, check that each is reachable by the AI, and report the ones that are declared but unused.
out_of_scope: Calling a tool (Tools does that), supplying the models and guardrails (World and Model Plumbing do that), and measuring how much code a connection needs (a metric of Tools).
milestones: 1. A declared enterprise integration is reachable by the AI and used (metric-integration-added-with-zero-code).
measures_of_success: Per-integration code changes (target 0); days from a hub listing an integration to a user connecting it; credential isolation checks all pass.
outputs: Which of the system's enduring integrations are accessible to the AI and which are used.
effects: Reads the registry's connection rows; writes nothing and makes no call.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Card Store
description: A small store that keeps cards, the hub's own memory unit, and finds them again by words or a tag.
purpose: Keep cards and find them again.
approach: Store each card under its id and search by every word of the query.
out_of_scope: Building the cards from files (Cards From Files does that) and choosing which cards a request needs (the Context Assembler does that).
milestones: 1. Every case passes: cards found again by words, nothing lost on a repeated add (metric-card-store).
measures_of_success: Cards found again by words; nothing lost on a second add of the same id.
parameters: The store location (in memory or one SQLite file).
inputs: A card to add, a card id, and a query with an optional tag and a result limit.
outputs: The id of an added card, a card or nothing for an id, the cards matching a query or a tag, whether a delete removed one, and the count.
effects: Writes and deletes cards in the store (a SQLite file when one is named); reads nothing else.
usage_notes: Default arm is local SQLite, in memory or one file.

name: Internal Context
description: Declares where the system's data lives and which World tool reads and writes it. The default is local files at a standard location, read and written through the File Editing tool. A system that keeps its data elsewhere declares that instead, with its own tool, through an adapter.
purpose: Let the AI know what a particular system knows, without the hub being written for that system: the declaration of where its data lives and whether each source belongs to the system or to a person, the configuration its tools need, and the run record the flow writes.
approach: Offer one declaration for each internal source, read it through an adapter, and keep what is read as cards.
out_of_scope: Reading or writing files and operations (World tools do that), retaining or recalling memories (Long-Term Memory does that), choosing the context a request needs (Subconscious does that) and proposing cards from files (Cards From Files does that).
milestones: 1. An internal source is declared once and its context reaches the AI (metric-internal-context).
measures_of_success: An internal source is declared once and its context reaches the AI.
outputs: The declared sources of the system's data, and the cards of its own context.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Intake Sources
description: Declares where this system's requests come from (a chat, a task queue, a place where meeting action items are written) and reads the requests waiting at each, handing each over once. The hub ships the folder queue; a system declares its own adapter.
purpose: Let a system say where its requests come from and read them, without the hub being written for that system.
approach: Do the one job of the solution by the best-measured implementation.
out_of_scope: Deciding who a request is from and what to do with it (Request Intake and the flow do that) and reading or writing the system's other data (Internal Context does that).
milestones: 1. Let a system say where its requests come from and read them, without the hub being written for that system. (authoritative metric metric-intake-sources).
measures_of_success: Let a system say where its requests come from and read them, without the hub being written for that system.
inputs: A source name and a limit.
outputs: The declared sources, and the requests waiting at one of them.
effects: Reads the declared source and removes each request it hands over.
